description: Access free medical check-ups, basic medicines, and vaccination services through Rural Health Units (RHUs) and barangay health centers across all 17 municipalities.
steps: Go to your nearest Rural Health Unit (RHU) or Barangay Health Center during clinic hours (Mon–Fri, 8 AM–5 PM).
First-timers will be issued an Individual Treatment Record (ITR).
For medicines, bring a doctor's prescription or referral.
For child immunization, visit on immunization day (typically Wednesdays) with your ECCD card.
For prenatal services, attend regular prenatal visits at your barangay health center.

description: Anti-rabies vaccination and wound management for individuals bitten by animals. Available at provincial and district hospitals and select RHUs.
steps: Go immediately to the nearest Animal Bite Treatment Center, RHU, or emergency room.
Present proof of Aklan residency (barangay certificate or valid ID).
Receive wound management and first dose of anti-rabies vaccine (free).
Follow up on subsequent doses as scheduled.
requirements: Valid ID or Barangay Certificate (proof of residency)

description: Free prenatal care, family planning services, and routine child immunization under the Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI) at RHUs and barangay health centers.
steps: Go to your nearest RHU or Barangay Health Center during clinic hours.
For prenatal: Bring previous prenatal records and valid ID. Staff will issue a prenatal record on first visit.
For child immunization: Visit on immunization day (typically Wednesdays, 8 AM–4 PM) with ECCD card.
For high-risk pregnancies: Request referral to DRSTMH OB-GYN department (24/7).
requirements: ECCD card (for child immunization — issued on first visit if none)

quickInfo.whoCanApply: Pregnant women and children under 12 months

sources.name: Department of Health — Expanded Program on Immunization

description: Free tuberculosis screening, diagnosis, and full course of anti-TB medicines under the National Tuberculosis Program (NTP) DOTS approach at RHUs across all 17 municipalities.
steps: Go to your nearest RHU or Barangay Health Center for TB screening.
If diagnosed with TB, you will be enrolled in the DOTS program.
Receive free anti-TB medicines and attend regular follow-up visits.
Complete the full course of treatment as prescribed.
